The mismatch is the path alone: the continuation control in the Code surface (`tools/code/ParkedTask.tsx` over `api/agentStream.ts`) posts `/api/{tool}/tasks/:taskId/continue`, so the implemented half of this row now has a caller, which it did not when the row was written.

The Code surface renders it (2026-09-21): RecoveryPanel, mounted in the main region when the selected task's run is interrupted, showing the bounded step tail with totals over all of it, the leftover checkout with what a discard would lose, and a two-step discard that mirrors the backend's own force rule. Resume is actioned from Code as of 2026-09-22: the panel takes `onResume` and hands the interrupted task's id to the Task composer, which focuses that region and starts the re-run through `POST /api/{tool}/run-task` — a re-run, not a continuation, because the continuation routes only move a parked run. Still `partial` for the one half that is left: Cowork and Design have no surface of their own yet, so only Code mounts the panel, and a host with no run-starter gets the verb with its reason and route in words rather than a disabled control.
Served by the queue rather than a separate /api/attention/approvals path: approvals arrive as items with kind approval_required, carrying the tool, task and the call that answers them.

Served by the queue rather than a separate /api/attention/interrupted path: interrupted runs arrive as items with kind interrupted. The TaskRun contract carries the state too since migration 020 (boot reconciliation writes interrupted, not error), so an interruption is discoverable in both places it is read.

Settings 2.5 slice 1: the provider ZDR editor in the Settings surface posts to this route (`api/providers.ts` `setProviderZdr`), and the read half remains the privacy line. The route's tri-state requestFlag and confirmed semantics are modelled in the form, not flattened to a boolean.

Enforced *and* disclosed since 2026-09-22. 1.36 classifies every provider failure and applies a cooldown per class (401/403 60m, 402 30m, 429 5m or Retry-After, 404 2m, 5xx 1m, network 30s) and the router skips a cooled provider; `ProviderPublic.cooldown` now carries the class, the `until` deadline, which length won (`table` or the provider's own `retry_after`) and the same sentence `cooldowns.ts` writes into switch events, on every provider read. `PrivacyIndicator` renders it at the point of send, including the fact that being skipped is not being disabled. The field is live in-memory state, so a cooldown clears with the process — which is the design (`cooldowns.ts` argues a persisted one would punish a key the user has since fixed), not a missing read.

Corrected in Settings 2.5 slice 1 (code wins): there is no `PUT /api/providers/:id/proxy` route and there never was — the egress proxy is a body field on `POST /api/providers` (create) and `PATCH /api/providers/:id` (update), parsed by `parseEgressProxy`. The Settings form sets it through `api/providers.ts` `createProvider`/`updateProvider`, treats the field as a secret (a proxy URL can carry a password), and reads back only the redacted form the provider object serves.

The spec asked for lineage by artifact id (`GET /api/artifacts/:id/versions`); the implementation serves it by artifact key (`GET /api/artifacts/versions?key=`, 1.39 A6), which is what the provenance panel calls. An id-based route would be a second way to ask the same question — artifact ids name a single version, while the lineage is the version list of one key.
